## Skill contract

- Discover skill identity, version, purpose, required capabilities, supported surfaces, input contract, output budget, and linked runtime commands.
- Fetch brief, standard, deep, or exact referenced sections on demand.
- Bind skill compatibility to pm package version, MCP protocol version, active extensions, and contract schema version.
- Generate or validate command examples against live contracts and execute negative controls in CI.
- Preserve repository-local overrides with explicit provenance and precedence.
- Measure tokens loaded, steps completed, refusal recovery, and stale-guidance escapes.
Skills over MCP: discoverable version-coherent pm workflows with progressive disclosure, capability requirements, and token budgets
Expose canonical pm skills through negotiated MCP extension contracts so agents can discover only the workflow guidance relevant to their role, surface, version, and current context budget.

Agents can list and fetch pm skills through a negotiated extension without loading unrelated bodies; Skill versions declare compatible pm, MCP, SDK, package, and contract versions and fail closed on drift; All CLI, SDK, MCP, package, testing, release, governance, and operator families have canonical skill routing or an explicit non-skill disposition; Examples and recovery commands are generated or validated against live runtime contracts in local and hosted CI; Token cost, completion success, stale guidance, and recovery closure are measured and ratcheted
Publish skills as structured versioned capabilities tied to runtime contracts instead of static duplicated prose
Agents receive complete current guidance without loading every pm command or maintaining harness-specific copies
The latest MCP ecosystem identifies Skills over MCP as an extension while the pm roadmap already requires all skills to cover CLI and SDK features through progressive disclosure
